title: Seams & Tangles Review (periodical run 7): area knots, dependency direction, ways in, rebuild readiness and change coupling — delta vs run 6 (11-commit window; the Home/task-page live-update work and three new files)
description:
<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="seams-tangles" -->

**Periodical: Seams & Tangles (corrective, run 7, delta against run 6).** Read how Harbour's **areas** depend on each other: where they knot, which way they point, whether each has a clear way in, how ready each is to be refactored or rebuilt behind a seam, and which areas keep **changing together**. Write a trend-framed, severity-ranked report, get an adversarial second-read, merge the report PR, mint at most \~3 one-move follow-ups, then conclude this task. **Review-only:** no code, config, guide (`scripts/code-shape/areas.json`) or doc edits beyond the report and its evidence files.

This run is also read as the **top-down reading for the Survey research** (`docs/plans/survey/log.md` and `docs/plans/survey/place-ledger.md` on branch `claude/cool-rubin-6acj5j`). That is context for what the numbers are used for, not extra scope: do not edit anything on that branch, and do not change what you report to fit it. If a finding bears on a place named in the place ledger, say so in one line and cross-link; the Survey's own docs are not this review's to change.

## Grounding (as found at mint time, `origin/main` = `2eb73ae07fb7297fc0fa057a6198aa8cbe901558`, 2026-11-05 06:00Z). Re-verify all of it; nothing here is a finding.

* **Repo:** `JKershaw/LinearViewer` (Harbour). PR and commit convention: `LIN-NNNN: <summary> (#PR)`. `ci-success` must be green before merging (`CLAUDE.md`).
* **Report convention:** `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-YYYY-MM-DD.md`, with raw tool JSON and guide copies in `docs/reviews/_evidence-YYYY-MM-DD/`. Today is 2026-11-05, so use `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-2026-11-05.md` and `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-05/`; check first that those names are free, and do not overwrite any 2026-11-04 file. `lib/periodical-report-gate.js` needs a comment on this task that cites a GitHub commit, PR or blob URL, plus the three second-read fields in one comment body, before Done.
* **Prior run (the baseline):** `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-2026-11-04-run6.md` (run 6, LIN-4231, Done, PR #2276, merge `43dd0d64764d34b8ea691f3dea58268b5adf1b8e`). It measured `d7ceb373444f9efbc027656132352d247535aa5e` against `5334c81a7207b9f2cc85ca429a2c6b18e1635c0e`, under both the old and HEAD guides, with evidence in `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-04-run6/`. Read it in full: what was measured, the changes, the trend table and the guide effect, its findings, change coupling, guide proposals, existing tickets, the follow-up decision, the second-read and the ledger with its stable names. Its open items and carried tickets are the list to re-check against the code, not against ticket state. Run 5 (`seams-tangles-review-2026-11-04.md`) is background.
* **The window.** `d7ceb373..2eb73ae0` is **11 commits over about 13 hours** (2026-11-04 19:04Z to 2026-11-05 06:00Z). Two are docs-only review reports (`43dd0d64` this series' run 6, `476d9ad4` the Drift & Coherence 11-04 run 2 report). Nine touch production (`lib routes public server.js`): LIN-4226 `c55f0fb3` (the cost read loads request records through a `requestSource`, LIN-4195 piece 4b), LIN-4234 `950113b1` (`usage-snapshot-intake` into INVENTORY; one source of collection names for both guards), LIN-4240 `279dcb0a` (`parseParkedWait` decides on the newest state-bearing entry), LIN-4241 `94195271` (settled-ruling guard, `409 ruling-settled`), LIN-4242 `ee8ec42e` (Waiting on you goes live: `home-waiting` fragment, shared keyed merge, one rulings tick), LIN-4243 `172f644a` (Home's Running and Up next follow the Waiting set), LIN-4151 `13fe24a0` (`/backlog` lead roots, one derivation for page and fold), LIN-4048 `c70b004c` (a finished task's page matches Home's run block), LIN-4143 `2eb73ae0` (the task page's ruling reads go through the live-run guard). Production is **44 files, +1,430 / -363** (verify with `git diff --shortstat d7ceb373 2eb73ae0 -- lib routes public server.js`). **Added:** `lib/ruling-settled.js`, `lib/waiting-section.js`, `public/home-placement.js`. **Deleted:** none seen. By `git diff`, `scripts/code-shape/` (the guide `areas.json` and the tools), `lib/runner-kit/` and `docs/runner-prompt.md` are **unchanged** in the window; `docs/architecture/source-map.md` and `docs/dispatch-integration.md` did change. Verify all of this. A short report is a genuine outcome if the import graph barely moved: do not pad it to match run 6's size.
* **Measure the number that matters most first:** the delta at the HEAD guide between `d7ceb373` and HEAD (files in scope, knot pairs and groups, cross-area link total, the catch-all file count, `lib/` -> `routes/` imports (the one written rule, expect 0), unresolved relative imports, parse failures), then each new file's area, direction and way in, then the Home and task-page seam.
* **Siblings and the seams between them:** **Drift & Coherence** (`drift-coherence-review-2026-11-04-run2.md`, LIN-4232, Done, merge `476d9ad4`; a run 3 is being minted alongside this task) owns decisions held in several places, file-level direction, file-level SCCs, text contracts and Simple Dispatcher's cross-repo contract. **Code Quality** (`code-quality-review-2026-11-04.md`) owns function size. **Stability** (`stability-review-2026-11-04.md`) owns churn and per-file change counts. **Simple Dispatcher** (`JKershaw/simple-dispatcher`) is flat CommonJS and outside what `seams.mjs` reads; say whether that still holds, and don't build a tool. Read the sibling reports' hand-offs to this review.
* **Parent context:** LIN-3549 (Done, code shape as a standard capability). `docs/runbooks/improvement-cycles.md` reads this report as a standing measure for the find-and-fix round.

## What to do

* **Audit the scope before executing.** Treat the scope above as a starting point to extend, not a checklist to stay inside. Before running the review, look for what is *in-remit but unlisted* and fold it in. Examples to check: the new files (`lib/ruling-settled.js`, `lib/waiting-section.js`, `public/home-placement.js`): which area the guide places each in, who imports them, whether each has a clear way in; the Home/task-page seam that LIN-4242, 4243, 4048 and 4143 all touched (a shared keyed merge, a home-waiting fragment, a live-run guard); `server.js` wiring; the browser seam (`window.X` globals, `scripts:` lists, `public/` load order) for the new `public/` file; the cost read after LIN-4226's `requestSource`; in-flight work (LIN-4195 and its pieces, PR #2185). A scope you could only shrink is suspect; the expected move is to widen it to what the remit actually reaches. Stay **broad in discovery but bounded in output**: the wider scope changes *what you examine*, not *what you report*. The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked (a clean, near-empty result is a genuine outcome), and the follow-up bound below stays as it is.
* **Read prior runs first. This review is trend-aware.** Find and read this review's earlier reports (confirm where they are recorded rather than trusting the path above), then frame every knot as a delta against the previous run: new, unchanged, improved, worsened or resolved, never a point-in-time snapshot. Keep run 6's stable ledger names (its ledger section) so the next run can compare mechanically. If a name no longer fits, retire it explicitly and say what replaced it. Tell apart a change that is **placement** (a file moved between areas, or the guide edited) from one that is **code** (an import added or removed): the guide, the measurement tools and the runner kit are unchanged in this window by `git diff` (verify), so a difference should be code, but confirm that before saying so.
* **Run the review.** Do not re-derive the dependency numbers by searching. Run `scripts/code-shape/seams.mjs <repoDir> <commit> [areaGuidePath]` at HEAD and at `d7ceb373444f9efbc027656132352d247535aa5e` **with the same area guide for both runs**, so a difference is code that moved and not a map that was edited. If the guide is unchanged, one guide for both runs is enough; say so. Record the full commit you measured. The tool reports facts only: links between areas, knots (pairs of areas that import each other both ways, and the groups they form) and each area's entry files, plus counts of what it could not read, which you must report rather than ignore. Everything else is your judgement, written as prose with no scores and no clustering: *wrong-way dependencies* (for example run logic importing page renderers), *hub modules* that much of the code imports and that import much of it, *whether each area has a clear way in* (its entry files, and whether callers use them), *rebuild readiness per area* (could it be refactored or rebuilt behind a seam, and what stops it) and *where the areas the import graph suggests differ from the guide's names*. Report changes since the previous report first. The guide is a guide, not a rule: propose edits to it in the report, record guide edits separately from code movement, and add no test, check or count that enforces it. The finding-classes above are **examples, not a limit. Discover the complete set for this remit from the repo; a class list is a floor to build on, never a ceiling to stay inside.**
* **Read change coupling beside the import coupling.** Run `scripts/code-shape/cochange.mjs <repoDir> <commit> --areas <guide> --days 60` at HEAD and at `d7ceb373…`, with the same area guide and the same window length for both runs, and report its top pairs beside the knots, with what moved between the two and against run 6's change-coupling figures. Report its counts of what it could not place (unmapped files, `shallow`) rather than ignore them. Say how much of the window the two runs share. Read a pair that changes together often yet has no link between its areas in `seams.mjs`'s output as a candidate seam: coupling the imports do not show, and a likely reason merges queue behind each other. State it as prose, with no score and nothing enforced. This is about pairs of areas only; per-file churn is the Stability Review's.
* **Mind the altitude. Do not double-flag.** This review reads the **direction and tangling between areas**. Decisions held in several places and the direction between individual files belong to the Drift & Coherence Review; function size belongs to the Code Quality Review; churn belongs to the Stability Review. Cross-link them where relevant; do not re-flag what they own.
* **Write an uncapped, trend-framed report** at `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-YYYY-MM-DD.md` (see Grounding for the name), evidence (raw JSON from every tool run, and byte copies of both guides) in `docs/reviews/_evidence-YYYY-MM-DD…/`. Confirm that convention before writing. If discovery genuinely turns up no such place, put the full report in a comment on this task instead of inventing a new location. The deliverable is a clear, severity-ranked report of everything found. Finding nothing, one thing or several are all valid; do not pad, cap or invent make-work. Ground each finding in the tool output at HEAD and the source it points to, not prior prose. Close with a compact trend ledger: each knot, hub and area under a stable, descriptive name, with its severity and its delta against the previous run, plus the change-coupling top pairs as rows with their run 5 values.
* **Mint a bounded set of follow-up tasks: highest-severity only.** Create at most the top \~3 by severity in Linear (fewer is fine; zero is valid when nothing rises to that bar, and in a window this size it usually will). Each is well-scoped: a title, and a description that carries the problem, why it matters, acceptance and file anchors. A fix idea is allowed but goes under an "Unvalidated idea" heading, so later stages treat it as a hypothesis. Leave each in its default state. **Before minting, search for an existing ticket already naming the same finding** (LIN-4154, LIN-4155, LIN-4193, LIN-3922, LIN-3923, LIN-3736/3737/3738/3555/2600, LIN-4195 and its pieces). If one exists, note it in the report instead of minting a duplicate. Record EVERY finding in the report, including the ones not promoted. Err toward under-creating, and weigh whether a new ticket will be worked before minting it, and say why.
* **Shape each follow-up as one move.** Scope every minted task to a single move (for example invert a dependency, give an area one way in, or move a shared piece down a level) and the seam it would open. The move itself and where the code ends up go under its "Unvalidated idea" heading. Do not mint a task that untangles several areas at once. A guide edit is a guide proposal in the report, not a code move.
* **Get a fresh-context adversarial second-read before this task can conclude. This is a required, structural step, not advice.** After the report and any follow-up tasks are written, and before the Done transition, a genuinely separate reader must answer one question cold: *"what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"* **Tier 1 (preferred):** a wholly separate session with no memory of this run. **Tier 2 (accepted fallback):** a fresh-context sub-agent carrying no memory of the report-writing turn. **Tier 3** (this same session re-reading its own report "from a cold stance") **is not accepted**; state which of Tier 1 or Tier 2 you used. Then post **one** comment on this task holding, together in a single body: `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`; `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO` (whether the reader's own answer differed from the report's top-ranked finding, independent of the verdict); and `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated` or `Disposition: no change`. The engine reads that comment and refuses Done until all three are present in one body. Copy the same three fields into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier, the question and the reader's answer in full. **AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude this task normally. A DISAGREE verdict is itself the escalation**, never a reason to leave this task open.
* **Merge your own report PR.** This task owns it. Once its required CI checks (`ci-success`) are green, merge it before the Done transition. The report is docs-only, so merging it yourself is safe. Only when merging is genuinely impossible (no merge permission, required checks still red) may this task conclude with the PR open, and then only as an explicit handoff naming the blocker in the closing comment. An open report PR is not a normal terminal state.
* **Then conclude this task. Do not leave it open.** Post a concise, severity-ranked summary of the report as a comment on this task, with a link to the merged report (a GitHub commit, PR or blob URL, which the report gate needs). Then move this task to Done. A review task left open is re-recommended indefinitely; the follow-up tasks carry the actionable work forward.
* **Stay review-only.** Producing the report changes no code, config, guide or secrets, and no docs beyond the report artifact and its evidence. An operator instruction to avoid touching files is about the code and docs *under review*; it does not override this task's own deliverable.
